subject: Staggered escrow + legal-hold flow for tailored retention windows
messages:
From: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@hearthstone.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@hearthstone.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial ask — staggered retention + legal hold

Dylan —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. A couple of compliance folks at Hearthstone asked if we can set up a staggered retention approach: 1) immediate short-term (30 days) for conversational logs, 2) medium-term (12 months) for model feedback metrics, and 3) long-term (36 months) for billing/contract artifacts, with the ability to apply legal holds per-customer or per-deal.

Key asks:
- Can the retention windows be configured per-route/model?
- How do legal holds interact with automated purge/escrow flows?
- What evidence can Redwood provide for an audit (timestamps, wipe certs)?

I attached a rough sketch of our desired flow. Can we get a proposal and an order-form-friendly SLA clause by EOD Monday?

—Maria
Compliance Manager
Hearthstone Analytics

Attachments: escrow-holdflow-diagram.png (image)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@hearthstone.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — staggered retention + legal hold

Maria —

Appreciate the clear bullets. Short answers up front: yes, per-route/model retention is supported; legal holds will suspend purge for affected keys/ids and route data to an escrow bucket if you opt in; and we can provide wipe certificates and an event log for every retention action.

We're attaching an initial proposal (redwood-tailored-retention-v3.pdf) that maps your 3 windows to config primitives, plus options for escrow handback and certified deletion. Monica — can you flag anything in the proposal that isn't order-form-ready? Karthik — can you weigh in on the legal-hold semantics (granularity & SLA impact)?

Next steps I propose:
1) Review this PDF internally (Monica/legal)
2) Align on whether escrow is automatic on hold or opt-in per account
3) Piece together a short SLA snippet (retention windows + hold handling) for Hearthstone's procurement team

We can also schedule a 30-min call Monday if helpful.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@hearthstone.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — staggered retention + legal hold

Following up after a quick internal sync. A few practical considerations for the order form language and operations: 

- Per-route retention: we can expose three named policies (short/medium/long) per account; customers can bind a route or model version to a named policy. We'll document default mappings and allow overrides via API.

- Legal hold semantics: when a hold is placed at the account or deal level, automatic purges are immediately suspended for affected objects. Objects under hold are flagged and replicated to a customer-specific escrow container if escrow is enabled in the order form. If escrow is NOT enabled, objects remain in our primary store but purges are disabled until release.

- Escrow handback: for accounts that pick escrow, we provide (a) a time-limited download token for the escrow snapshot, (b) a checksum manifest, and (c) a signed deletion certificate when the escrow object is released and wiped from Redwood's systems.

- Audit evidence: we can provide an event log (immutable) with timestamps for retention-policy changes, hold placements/releases, purge attempts, and wipe confirmations. We'll include a sample schema in the appendix of the PDF.

Order-form wording (draft snippet):
"Redwood will support per-route retention policies with configurable short/medium/long windows as defined in Appendix A. Legal holds supersede scheduled purges; while a legal hold is in effect Redwood will suspend deletion of affected data and, where escrow has been purchased, replicate affected objects to a customer-specific escrow container. Upon release of a legal hold Redwood will resume scheduled deletions and, where applicable, execute escrow handback or certified deletion as defined in Appendix B."

Open questions for Hearthstone:
- Do you want escrow to be opt-in per hold, or a global account-level election?
- What retention windows do you want as defaults (we recommended 30 / 12 / 36 as Maria suggested)?

Happy to iterate rapidly on the order-form language if you can confirm the escrow election.

Cheers,
Monica
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@hearthstone.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — staggered retention + legal hold

Maria —

Quick legal/ops clarification from our side: for auditability we recommend (and will include in the SLA appendix) the following minimums:
1) Hold metadata must include initiating user, hold scope (account/deal/route/object), timestamp, and expected release trigger (manual/timebound/court order).
2) Escrow snapshots are encrypted with a customer-specific key; Redwood will provide proof-of-possession logs for key usage during handback.
3) Purge suspension does not absolve the customer of obligations to notify relevant parties; Redwood will retain a copy in escrow only if escrow is elected in the order form.

If Hearthstone prefers escrow-by-default for holds, that will be reflected as an extra line item on the order form and will change lead times for provisioning. Otherwise, opt-in escrow keeps costs simpler.

I'll add the short legal-hold semantics paragraph to the SLA snippet and send a one-page summary to Maria.

—Karthik
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
